info.title: Fractal Flame API
info.description: Backend API for storing, searching, and serving fractal flame configurations

200.description: Flame with v2 config blob + root transforms

404.description: Flame not found or not forkable

200.description: Current user's resource usage and limits

404.description: No library entry for this hash

200.description: List all available variations (lightweight; no shaders or parameter schema)

AnimationRef.description: Lightweight reference to an animation — used in flame responses.

CreateFlamePalette.description:
Embedded palette in a flame request. `hash` is optional if `color_data`/
`stops` are present (server computes hash, upserts content); if no content
is provided, the server requires `hash` to already exist in `palette_data`.
`name` is the flame-specific display name, denormalized onto the flame row.

config.description:
Opaque to the server end-to-end. The Phase 2 dual-write path parses
this internally into `FlameConfigBlob` to populate the v1 typed
columns alongside the v2 JSONB column, but unknown fields the client
adds round-trip via the JSONB column untouched.

FlamePalette.description:
Embedded palette in a flame response. Always carries the hash + the
flame's display name; content fields are populated from `palette_data`.

FlameResponse.description:
v2 wire response shape. Everything that's not identity / engagement /
palette lives inside `config` (the opaque JSON blob). Root-flame
transforms ride alongside `config` in their own array; subflames + their
transforms live INSIDE `config.subflames[]`.

render_mode.description:
Top-level mirror of `config.render_mode` so list + detail responses
have a consistent shape (FlameListItem already exposes it at the
top level). The same value also lives inside `config` for clients
that prefer to read it from the blob.

PaletteContent.description:
Public palette content, returned by `GET /api/palettes/{hash}` and
embedded in flame responses.

SubmitPaletteRequest.description:
Submit palette content. Server computes the hash from `color_data`+`stops`,
upserts into `palette_data`, and (if `nickname` is set) adds the palette
to the caller's library with that nickname.

nickname.description: If set, also adds the palette to the caller's library with this name.

SubmitPaletteResponse.description:
Response from `POST /api/palettes`. `added_to_library` is true when the
caller asked for `nickname` AND a new library entry was created (existing
entries are not overwritten — use the library endpoints for that).

TransformV2Wire.description:
What a single transform looks like on the wire — both in
`CreateFlameRequest.transforms[]` and `FlameResponse.transforms[]`.

`data` is opaque to the server end-to-end: stored as JSONB in
`transforms.data`, served back verbatim. The client owns the shape.

UpsertUserPaletteRequest.description: `PUT /api/users/me/palettes/{hash}` body — adds or updates a library entry.

UserProfileResponse.description: API response combining user_profiles fields with display_name from users table.

aliases.description:
Foreign-app names that resolve to this variation on `.flame` import
(Apophysis/JWildfire `linear3D` → our `linear`).

authors.description:
Historical attribution — the designers, in order. **Not** a foreign key
to `users`; these are people, not accounts.

description_plain.description:
`description` with markdown syntax stripped, for clients without a
markdown renderer. Absent falls back to showing `description` raw,
which degrades readably.

features.description:
The §6.1 capability array — **authoritative for all thirteen flags**.
A payload carrying `features` supersedes the legacy bools below rather
than merging with them, and an unrecognised name is dropped with a
warning client-side rather than rejecting the variation, so adding a
capability is never a breaking change in the server→client direction.

needs_rng.description:
Legacy signature-shaping bools, superseded by `features` but still
served during the transition. `needs_transform` was `needs_affine`
until migration 76; the client has carried a serde alias throughout.

plot_emits.description:
`Feature::PlotEmits(u8)` — the one engine feature carrying a payload,
so it cannot ride the `features` string array.

`None` is the *only* encoding of absence. **`0` means "does not emit"**,
not "emits zero", so a stored `0` would be a second spelling of `None`
— and `plot_emits.is_some()`, which reads as "has the feature", would
be wrong for exactly that input. Migration 75 rejects it.

state_count.description:
Per-(thread, xform, variation) f32 slots persisted across the inner
iteration loop, paired with the WGSL that seeds them beyond zero-fill.

Uncapped: state lives in a separate buffer sized dynamically from the
flame, so it neither joins the packed-parameter sum nor needs a ceiling.

VariationListItem.description:
Lightweight shape used by `GET /api/variations`. Omits `parameters` and
the shader sources so a full catalog list stays small; clients hit
`GET /api/variations/{name}` for full data.

The bar for a field here is that a **browse/select decision** can be made
from it. Engine wiring (`phase`, `features`, `needs_rng`, `needs_transform`,
`writes_color`, `init_param_count`, and `state_count` when it lands) does
not qualify — registration always happens from the detail payload, so
wiring on the list is bytes with no consumer, fetched for the whole corpus
under the manifest-driven catalog.

Those five were trimmed on 2026-07-31 after the client confirmed nothing
declares them and nothing uses `deny_unknown_fields`. This shape is now
the client's documented §2 plus `has_shader_3d`.
See docs/api-shared-resources-server.md §1.2.

downloadable.description:
Whether a client may fetch and register this variation at runtime.

Not "has a shader". `subflame_wf` has a real 2D shader on the client —
it calls `subflame_iterate` and reads the subflame storage buffers —
it is simply **built-in-only by nature**, so there is nothing servable
to store. Saying `downloadable: false` states that truthfully while
keeping the row in the catalog for the browsing app and the panel.

Earns its place by the same rule as `has_shader_3d`: "don't try to
fetch this" is exactly a browse-or-select decision. It also underwrites
the download contract — **if it's downloadable, it has a shader the
client can use for its category**:

* any category → `shader_2d` required. A NULL there would reach the
  emit loop's `else { continue }` and silently contribute nothing.
* `only_3d` → `shader_3d` suffices. The engine removes these from the
  active set in 2D builds *before any source lookup*, so a 2D body is
  never read and requiring one would mean dead data that looks
  meaningful (migration 74).

One-directional: see `variations_downloadable_has_shader` for why a
shader won't stay *sufficient* either (name-gated helper libraries).

has_shader_3d.description:
Whether a dedicated 3D shader exists. Derived (`shader_3d IS NOT
NULL`), not stored.

Earns its place on the list because it drives a decision made *before*
download: the client's shader builder **skips a variation with no
`shader_3d` entirely** in 3D flames, so it contributes nothing and the
user meets it as a variation that renders blank. (The skip is
deliberate — an earlier 2D-pass-through fallback masked vec2/vec3
shader-validation crashes.) On the manifest the panel can mark it
"2D only" up front instead.

Contrast `shader_init`, which is deliberately *not* here: a missing
init shader has no valid form (the slots are allocated either way and
read as zeros), so it's a publish-time invariant — already enforced by
`variations_init_pair_check` — rather than something to advertise.

VariationParameter.description:
Metadata describing one parameter a variation accepts. Stored as a JSONB
array on `variations.parameters` and decoded on reads.
